Best tips for people feeling "stuck" with mobile apps:

1. People always flex revenue. 
They dont show the ad spend. Don't get discouraged seeing 'gurus' hitting $100,000 MRR. They are full of shit

2. Failure is beautifully unpersonal. 
Try to understand why you're failing and what you can do to fix it. Nobody has magic powers. Failure is an objective sign you're doing something wrong, so there is an objective way to make it right.

Examples:
I have no downloads -> start marketing

I have low views -> Compare your content with succesful competitors and improve

I have high views but no downloads -> Fix CTA / app positioning inside creative

My retention sucks -> Implement user loops / change target audience

I tried for a year but still no revenue -> Switch apps

Solutions should be systematic. Don't rely on intuition.

3. Take sundays off. 
Trust me. I dont care if you work 16 hours everyday, as long as you have ONE day free for your personal life

4. Don't look so serious. 
Smile a little. There will be a day where you become a millionaire, and you'll look back wishing you could cherish the struggles you are currently experiencing as a small entrepreneur

5. Business cannot substitute an unsatisfactory personal life. 
Find a hobby, find a purpose or you'll end up a depressed millionaire

6. Be open-minded. 
Learning is fun. Look at what others are doing, ask for help and be HUMBLE. Help others even if they don't benefit you directly. Connect with people. Criticize yourself first before you criticize others. Mindful introspection is key. Mindfulness will be more valuable to you than 10K MRR

Make sure you have older friends.

Young people (myself included (when I was young)) have a tendency to think of older people as "not like us" or out of touch.

Older people should have high-agency younger friends to keep them on their toes and remind them to keep being courageous and unfearful.

I watched Ramayana yesterday at IMAX 3D; ideally, an IMAX 2D option would exist, since 3D darkens every scene. 

Regarding the film, the criticism feels excessive; it is decent, yet the main issue is a rushed pace that lacks the satisfaction found in series like “Sampoorna Ramayana”. 

Nobody talks about Ravindra Jain’s magic, which made these epics more moving and shaped their atmosphere. 

Every character performed well in my view, and the visuals are strong, though I do not prioritize them - the older version people prefer was never about VFX. The music is decent and improves with repetition, but I miss Ravindra Jain’s touch most of all. 

Dialogue is sparse apart from Ravana, and Lakshman’s humour feels hurried. Major events like the swayamvar and the journey from Ayodhya to Chitrakoot deserved more time.
